answer: A nebula of throwaway identities collapses when each agent must anchor its reputation to a refundable stake locked in a public registry: creating an identity costs a basalt-hard bond that is slashed if peers catch it attesting falsely, while honest work slowly earns the bond back with interest. One operator running a thousand sock puppets must fund a thousand bonds, so the marginal cost of each fake exceeds what it can earn, while a single honest agent pays once and keeps working.
